PROJECT PLANNING

Build a Ground Engineering Responsibility Matrix That People Will Use

A simple ownership map can prevent gaps between specialist packages.

In this insight

List activities at the interfacesSeparate doing from approvingAdd timing and dependenciesKeep the matrix aligned with realityFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

List activities at the interfaces

Start with the points where work passes between teams: site readiness, design information, approvals, working space, support installation, excavation release, water management and handover. A responsibility matrix becomes useful when it addresses these real activities rather than broad headings such as construction. Describe the output expected from each party so ownership can be understood in practical terms.

Separate doing from approving

The party preparing a document may not be the party checking or authorising it. Show those roles separately. Include the client, main contractor, specialist contractors, designers and relevant third parties where necessary. Avoid assigning responsibility to a generic project team label that does not identify who can act. The matrix should support, not replace, the contractual allocation of obligations.

Add timing and dependencies

A responsibility without a required date may remain unresolved until it blocks work. Link key outputs to programme milestones and identify the information needed to produce them. This turns the matrix into a coordination tool rather than a static appendix. Review high-risk or time-critical interfaces at mobilisation and when the sequence changes.

Keep the matrix aligned with reality

Update the matrix when packages, personnel or design responsibilities change. Obtain agreement from the affected parties and retain the revision history. Use it during meetings to resolve ownership questions quickly. If an action repeatedly falls between teams, revise the description or allocation rather than allowing the same discussion to recur. A short, maintained matrix is more valuable than an exhaustive document that no one trusts.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Describe specific interface outputs.
  • Separate preparation, review and authorisation.
  • Update ownership when the delivery structure changes.
